words.said: Your six months of voice notes point to 6 changes in how we work
words.how: Page opens with the punchline box 'Your six months of voice notes point to 6 changes in how we work. Here they are.' and the six-change table follows.
Change 1 is a fresh-reader test: a fresh reader must say in one sentence what is being asked, with 41 notes.

words.said: Yes: run it on all notes
words.how: His 'Yes: run it on all notes' is about the run itself; the card says all 421 notes were read in three passes.

words.said: I don't know what you're asking. I don't understand your question, bro ... my expectation was, what changes were we gonna drive into the Epic Spine? ... 10,000 times more clear, please.
words.how: Clarity test for every card and question is the first change, and the page shows the test at the top of the table.

words.said: ask questions more clearly in general
words.how: His request for clearer questions in general is about the ask style, not the six-change page; the card's rule 1 covers it indirectly.

visual.summary: Both widths open with the punchline box under the title, show the six-change table with counts and quotes, fit without sideways scroll, and end with the detail block; the card's ✗ line declares nothing is made yet.
